approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would take money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for government services that are not routine annual services.

It would provide about five-twelfths of the estimated 2022-23 annual funding for these non-routine services, with larger amounts for entities like the Department of Health that have high early-year spending or COVID-19 costs.
The explanatory memorandum notes the remaining seven-twelfths plus new budget measures would come in a later bill.
The bill would appropriate funds from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for non-ordinary annual services.
It would set the appropriation at roughly five-twelfths of the estimated annual amount, with some entities receiving more.
It would keep these appropriations separate from ordinary annual services to follow constitutional rules.
Parliament, government entities such as the Department of Health, and the Consolidated Revenue Fund are affected.

The majority voted against a request for an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2022-03-30.20.2), which means the amendment failed. The Supply Bill (No. 1) 2022-2023 and related bills seek over $80 billion in interim appropriations to fund normal government business and extended COVID-19 response measures for the first five months of 2022‑23. The bill includes a $2.4 billion advance to the finance minister—$2 billion earmarked for COVID-19 and $400 million for other urgent expenditure—with enhanced transparency and opposition concurrence required for advances over $1 billion.

The bill seeks $10.7 billion in appropriations for capital works, payments to states and territories, and equity injections for the first five months of 2022‑23, including extended COVID‑19 response measures. It also provides a $3.6 billion advance to the Finance Minister—$3 billion for COVID‑related expenditure and $600 million for other urgent spending—while returning the general advance to pre‑pandemic settings.

The Supply Bill (No. 1) 2022-2023, Supply Bill (No. 2) 2022-2023 and Supply (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2022-2023 seek authority to appropriate just over $91 billion from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the first five months of 2022-23. The bills provide interim funding to ensure continuity of programs and services from 1 July 2022 until annual appropriation bills pass, and contain no new budget measures.

The Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2022‑2023 proposes $13.3 billion in spending, including $7.7 billion for Defence, $3.9 billion for infrastructure, and $495 million for Airservices Australia, with a $3 billion Advance to the Finance Minister for COVID‑19 measures and $600 million for other urgent expenditure.
